 Letter: In-person voting infuses pride and responsibility

 Share on Facebook

 MARCO GARCIA / SPECIAL TO THE STAR-ADVERTISER
 A view of the early voting at Honolulu Hale on Friday, Oct. 23.
 In the past, voters eagerly checked in at a polling location, made their selections behind a curtain and proudly turned in their ballot. These days it’s done by mail, with obvious differences.
 The more weeks we hang onto them, the more mundane they become. Like filing taxes.
 Some ask their poker table buddies which names to pick — almost like betting on a horse race. Hopefully, spilled food doesn’t make the ballots sticky and later jam the counting machines. Sometimes ballots are misplaced or lost. Voting during a bubble bath while talking story to an artificial intelligence friend is probably not the best way to make political decisions of an important nature.
 Silliness aside, should we return to the traditional polling center method, to instill civic pride and personal responsibility back into our valued voting process? Casting ballots should be at a solemn and revered location of honor among peers.
 John Burns 
 Wahiawa
